content_sections.body: In this lesson, focus on present relevance, a supported opinion, and a tactful qualification. Notice how the ideas about joining a running group are linked so that the listener can follow the speaker's meaning.
content_sections.title: Notice the language

content_sections.body: I have belonged to a running group since January. I think it has improved my routine because I exercise regularly, although I understand that group activities do not suit everyone.
content_sections.title: Context and meaning

content_sections.body: Prepare a three-sentence response about joining a running group. Include the lesson language, one concrete detail, and a clear link between your ideas.
content_sections.title: Guided use

items: The speaker gives no view or experience.
The speaker reaches the opposite conclusion.
exercises.prompt: Choose the statement that best matches the message about joining a running group.
Complete this Review: experiences and change sentence with a suitable linker: I have experience of this topic, ____ I can explain my view clearly.

Read the text: "I have belonged to a running group since January. I think it has improved my routine because I exercise regularly, although I understand that group activities do not suit everyone." Then answer: When did the speaker join the group?
Give a connected response about joining a running group, then respond politely to one follow-up view.
exercises.rubric: States a clear experience or viewpoint.; Supports the main idea with a relevant detail.; Links ideas clearly and responds tactfully.

objectives: Review experience, opinion, and tactful response targets.

constraints: Keep transcript private until the first answer.
Ask exactly one question before revealing it.
Use no media; use only the supplied transcript.
listening.goal: Identify the main point and supporting detail about joining a running group.
listening.instruction: Listen once to a short message about joining a running group. Answer one question before seeing the transcript, then listen again for the linking language.

pronunciation.goal: Use sentence stress to make the main viewpoint about joining a running group clear.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the key message about joining a running group aloud. Stress the word that carries the main contrast or new information, first slowly and then naturally.

constraints: Use at most four tutor turns.
End after the learner has supported and clarified the main point.
speaking.goal: Complete a connected exchange about joining a running group.
speaking.instruction: Discuss joining a running group with the tutor. Give your experience or opinion, support it, and respond tactfully to one different view.

constraints: Do not replace the learner draft.
writing.goal: Write a supported B1 response about joining a running group.
writing.instruction: Write 5-6 connected sentences about joining a running group. Include a clear main point, a reason or example, and a tactful contrast. Submit your draft first.
